22.​Add after paragraph 66 and renumber (London - Walthamstow) 
 
While fundamentally remaining on the US’ leash, the economic power of China will 
also have a growing influence upon British capitalism. Imports of goods and services 
from China have grown to new heights in the past 5 years. Chinese and Hong 
Kong-linked capital has also entered major areas of British infrastructure, including 
electricity, water, gas, and nuclear power. China also remains an important UK export 
and investment destination, and the stock of British foreign direct investment towards 
China rose by 78.9% between 2023 and 2024. All this means that British capitalism will 
have to somehow submit to the US’ anti-China ​ agenda while also seeking more 
investments, markets, and technology from China, a deeply contradictory position. 
 
CC recommendation: Accept​
 
23.​Amend paragraph 94 (Durham) 
 
As they get closer to power, more and more Tories are defecting to Reform, welcomed with 
open arms and a grin by Nigel Farage. This can only help him in his mission to court big 
business and show the ruling class he can manage capitalism, but it undermines his 
anti-establishment image and causes discontent in the party’s ranks. Already, demagogic 
splitaways with more hardline right-wing stances on deportations and "anti-woke 
politics" such as Restore Britain have attracted layers within Reform disappointed 
with this pivot to the establishment. 
 
CC recommendation: Accept 
 
24.​Amend paragraph 94 (Chelmsford) 
 
As they get closer to power, more and more Tories are defecting to Reform, welcomed with 
open arms and a grin by Nigel Farage. Additionally, Reform has dropped its populist 
policies of nationalisation of both the water and energy industries. This can only help 
Farage in his mission to court big business and show the ruling class he can manage 
capitalism, but it undermines his anti-establishment image and causes discontent in the 
party’s ranks. 
 
CC recommendation: Accept  
 
 
25.​Add after paragraph 94 and renumber (Leeds Arts) 
 
This has led to fractures already within this heterogenous cross-class coalition. The 
formation of Restore Britain to the right of Farage, under ex-Reform MP Rupert Lowe, 
is an early indicator of this volatility. It would take massive events however to 
transform this fringe grouping into a serious factor in British politics. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject
